All other checkpoints regarding head, body shape, and stance are correctly marked as present. The expert classifier confirms 'wombat' as the top class, supporting the alignment verdicts.
artifact_review: The Router identified a severe texture anomaly in the foreground (blue-grey spiky objects) with severity 4. I confirm this is a major hallucination; these objects resemble metallic shards or digital noise rather than biological scat or rocks. The Router also noted minor fusion at the paws (severity 2). Upon reviewing the topology mask, there is significant fragmentation/islanding near the rear right leg and the nose area, suggesting the segmentation model struggled with boundary definition in those spots, likely due to low contrast or melting. This supports the presence of structural artifacts beyond just the foreground debris. The perceptual auditor found no global distortion, but the local semantic error in the foreground is catastrophic for realism.
alignment_reasoning: 8/9 checkpoints passed. The failure on claw visibility is justified by image quality and foreground obstruction. Expert classifier strongly confirms wombat identity. Score reflects high anatomical accuracy despite one unresolvable detail.
artifact_reasoning: Severe foreground hallucination (metallic/spiky debris instead of scat/rocks) dominates the artifact score. Minor limb-ground fusion and topology mask fragmentation at the rear/nose indicate additional structural weaknesses. The foreground error is visually jarring and biologically implausible.

self_reflection_notes: Scores remain unchanged after reflection. Alignment (4.35) is consistent with 8/9 checkpoints passing and strong classifier confirmation; the single missing detail (claws) is legitimately obscured. Artifact score (1.85) appropriately reflects the severe foreground hallucination (severity 4) which is the dominant defect, compounded by minor fusion and mask fragmentation. No contradictions found between reasoning and scores. Expert evidence was fully utilized: classifier confirmed identity, topology mask revealed subtle boundary issues missed by visual inspection alone, and perceptual auditor's null result was correctly interpreted as not negating the semantic foreground error. Leniency bias was avoided by independently verifying the claw checkpoint failure and mask fragmentation. Harshness bias was avoided by not over-penalizing the minor fusion given the already severe foreground artifact.
